In /opt/nxeon-staging, build a "sent email preview" feature for the Cold Email admin section, matching the design of the EXISTING regular Email Log viewer exactly, per explicit user request ("should be similar to our existing email logs page in the admin portal").

## Reference to copy the pattern from
- `components/admin/EmailLogViewer.tsx` — the exact UI pattern to replicate: a stats row (3 cards), a table of sent messages with a "Preview" button per row, and a modal (rendered via `createPortal` into `document.body`) showing the email in a **sandboxed iframe** (`sandbox=""`) with the tracking pixel stripped out via a regex (`stripTrackingPixel`) so previewing never counts as a real open. Copy this exact interaction pattern — table + modal + sandboxed iframe + pixel-stripping — for cold email.
- `app/admin/logs/page.tsx` — the page that feeds `EmailLogViewer` its data; follow the same "fetch rows server-side, pass to a client component" structure.

## Background (already investigated by a prior read-only pass)
Cold email currently does NOT store the actual rendered content of a sent email — only the campaign-level template. Relevant files:
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — `model ColdSend` (~line 4065): has `id`, `campaignId`, `contactId`, `stepId`, `status`, `inboxId`, `sentAt`, `messageId`, `error`, `trackingToken`, `openedAt`/`openCount`/`clickedAt` — but NO subject/body fields.
- `worker/coldemail.ts` (~line 400-430): the send loop. It calls `buildMessage({...})` from `lib/coldemail/sender.ts` to render the personalized subject/HTML/text (with tracking injected), hands it to nodemailer, then the rendered content is discarded — never written back to `ColdSend`.
- `lib/coldemail/sender.ts` — `buildMessage()` — read this to see exactly what it returns (subject, html, text, or similar shape).

IMPORTANT — schema/tree caution: other background agents may be concurrently editing `prisma/schema.prisma` and other shared files in this same staging tree (a scheduled improvement agent and other feature work are active). Before editing `prisma/schema.prisma`, re-read it fresh to find the current, real `ColdSend` model block rather than trusting only the line numbers above (they may have shifted). Make your schema edit purely additive.

## What to build

### 1. Schema: persist rendered content at send time
Add to `ColdSend`: `subjectSent String?` and `bodyHtmlSent String?` (nullable — legacy/pre-feature sends won't have this, which is fine and expected; the UI should handle rows where these are null gracefully, e.g. "Preview not available for this send").

### 2. Worker: write the rendered content when actually sending
In `worker/coldemail.ts`, right where `buildMessage()` is called and the resulting `msg` is used to actually send via nodemailer, include `subjectSent: msg.subject` and `bodyHtmlSent: msg.html` (or whichever exact property names `buildMessage()`'s return type uses — check it) in the `db.coldSend.update(...)` call that already runs after a successful send (find the existing success-path update near where `status: "SENT"` or similar gets set, alongside `sentAt`/`messageId` — add the two new fields to that SAME update rather than adding a new separate write).

### 3. Admin UI: a viewer matching EmailLogViewer.tsx's exact pattern
Where to put it: the user wants "all the email previews that are sent" visible — the most natural home is a new sub-tab/section within the existing cold-email campaign detail page (`app/admin/coldemail/campaigns/[id]/...` — find the exact existing file and its current tab structure, e.g. Overview/Campaigns tabs mentioned by the user) OR a new top-level `/admin/coldemail/sent` page if that fits the existing nav pattern better (check `app/admin/coldemail/` directory structure and how "Cold Email" appears in the admin sidebar nav to decide the more consistent placement — follow whatever pattern the existing Cold Email admin section already uses for Leads/Campaigns/Sending identity/etc. sub-pages).

Build a new component (e.g. `components/admin/coldemail/SentEmailViewer.tsx`) that is a close structural copy of `EmailLogViewer.tsx`:
- Stats row: total sent (with a preview available), open rate, click rate — reuse `ColdSend`'s existing `openedAt`/`openCount`/`clickedAt`/`clickCount` fields for the rates (same calculation pattern as `EmailLogViewer`).
- Table columns: Time (sentAt), To (contact's email — join `contactId` to get it), Subject (`subjectSent`), Status, Opened, Clicked, Preview button.
- Modal: sandboxed iframe (`sandbox=""`) rendering `bodyHtmlSent` with the SAME tracking-pixel-stripping regex logic as `stripTrackingPixel()` in `EmailLogViewer.tsx` — copy that function or extract it to a shared util if that's cleaner, your call, but the behavior must be identical (never let a preview count as a real open).
- Data fetch: a new server-side query (in the campaign detail page's server component, or a new server action) that pulls `ColdSend` rows for a campaign (or globally, if you go the `/admin/coldemail/sent` route) with `subjectSent`/`bodyHtmlSent` not null, joined to the contact's email. Respect the same admin auth gating pattern already used elsewhere in `app/admin/coldemail/*` (check an existing page there for the exact `requireArea`/`requireAdmin` call and mirror it).
- Filter/scope: if built as a campaign-detail sub-tab, scope to that campaign's sends only. If built as a new global page, add a campaign-name/id filter dropdown so it doesn't become an unusable firehose across all campaigns.

## Verification
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` after the schema change and after the UI is built; fix errors before finishing.
- Run `npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss` in `/opt/nxeon-staging` after the schema edit.
- Do NOT run `npm run build` — another process may hold the build lock in this shared tree.
- This only affects FUTURE sends (existing already-sent `ColdSend` rows will have null `subjectSent`/`bodyHtmlSent` — that's expected and fine, no backfill needed/possible since the original rendered content was never stored).

Report back: exact file paths touched/created, where you placed the new UI (campaign sub-tab vs new top-level page and why), and confirm the tracking-pixel-stripping behavior matches `EmailLogViewer.tsx` exactly.

I'm planning to build the SentEmailViewer component modeled closely on EmailLogViewer.tsx, incorporating an embedded campaign filter dropdown and reusing the existing Badge tones and primitives like PageHeader. I'm sketching out its props, including rows and campaign data.

Now I'm reconsidering the data-fetching instructions, which say to pull ColdSend rows only where subjectSent/bodyHtmlSent are non-null, yet also say the UI should gracefully handle null previews with a "Preview not available" message -- these two requirements seem to conflict, so I need to reread the spec carefully to reconcile whether filtering happens at the query level or the UI should show all sent rows regardless.

This resolves it: I'll fetch all SENT ColdSend rows for the scope, keeping ones with null subjectSent/bodyHtmlSent, and show "not available" for those preview buttons. The stats row will report total sent (as denominator, matching EmailLogViewer's rate calculations) alongside a separate "preview available" count of rows with non-null bodyHtmlSent, plus open and click rates.

For the first stat card, I'm deciding to display "Sent (with preview)" as previewAvailable count out of sentTotal, e.g. "42 of 50", mirroring the subtext pattern EmailLogViewer uses.

I think the null-handling instruction is really about defensive coding rather than including non-preview rows in the main list — if either subjectSent or bodyHtmlSent is missing, I should just show "Preview not available" text instead of a Preview button, rather than crashing. But the deeper UX question remains: does the user want strictly preview-available sends listed, or all sent emails with previews shown where available?

I'll go with querying only rows where both fields are non-null, matching the "Data fetch" instruction directly, while still defensively handling any partial-null edge case in the render logic. That means the "total sent (with a preview available)" stat card can just equal the row count, since every fetched row already has a preview by definition.

For open/click rates, I'll follow the same pattern as EmailLogViewer: count rows with openedAt/clickedAt present, dividing by the same filtered row set that's displayed, so the denominator stays consistent with what's shown on screen.

Then for table columns, I'll stick to the literal spec — Time, To, Subject, Status, Opened, Clicked, Preview — though since this is a global page across campaigns, I'm weighing whether to add a Campaign column for clarity, since the filter dropdown alone might not be enough to distinguish rows at a glance.

Since the status will always show as sent given the data path, I'll just add a defensive "SENT" filter to the query even though it's redundant with the existing logic. Now I need to decide where the data fetch function lives—likely inline in the page similar to the pattern used in the logs page.

I'm going with an inline async page component that fetches campaigns and sent rows together via Promise.all, following the campaign detail page's structure. Writing the page setup...

Mapping in open/click tracking data, then rendering the page with a header and a sent-email viewer component that shows a sandboxed preview of each message alongside campaign filtering.

I'm reconsidering whether to keep the html field nullable in the type definition, since even though the current query filters out nulls, a future caller might reuse this component with unfiltered data, so it's safer to handle the null case gracefully as originally instructed.

This actually resolves things better: querying all sent rows regardless of preview fields, then handling nulls gracefully in the UI, explains why the "Preview not available" instruction exists in the first place — it wouldn't make sense if those rows were filtered out. I'll go with querying all sent ColdSend rows scoped to the campaign, without filtering on subject/body fields, and handle nulls in the UI display.

Now I'm finalizing the stats layout: card 1 shows total sent with a subtext noting how many have previews available, and cards 2/3 compute open/click rates using the total sent count as denominator, matching the same pattern used in EmailLogViewer. For the table, I'm laying out columns for time, recipient, subject, campaign (if global), status, opened, clicked, and preview, falling back to a placeholder when the subject wasn't captured.

For legacy rows where the subject wasn't stored, I'm showing a dash with a tooltip explaining the preview wasn't captured before this feature existed, and disabling the preview button when there's no HTML body saved. I'm reusing the same tracking-pixel stripping regex from the transactional email path so previews render cleanly without the tracking image embedded.

The task really means to preserve the same logic of stripping any img tag pointing at the tracking pixel, just adapted to cold email's differing URL path—so I'll extract that regex logic into a shared utility in lib/email-render.ts, which is already imported in sender.ts, rather than duplicating the function.

I found the exact pixel URL pattern in sender.ts, confirming the regex target should match `/api/coldemail/track/open/`. Rather than extracting a shared utility, I'll keep it simple and write a self-contained local function in SentEmailViewer.tsx, leaving EmailLogViewer.tsx untouched to avoid any risk of disturbing a concurrently-edited component.

Since other agents may be editing shared files simultaneously, I'm avoiding shared utilities and duplicating the logic locally instead, with adapted regex and a comment referencing EmailLogViewer's implementation for behavior parity. +          subjectSent: msg.subject,
+          bodyHtmlSent: msg.html,
         },
       });
       await db.emailEvent.create({ data: { sendId: s.id, type: "SENT" } });

Cold-email "sent email preview" feature is built and verified. Summary of changes in `/opt/nxeon-staging`:

**Schema** (`prisma/schema.prisma`, purely additive, ~line 4082 in `model ColdSend`):
- Added `subjectSent String?` and `bodyHtmlSent String?` to `ColdSend`, nullable so legacy sends and other in-flight schema edits from concurrent agents were untouched.
- Ran `npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss` — synced successfully, client regenerated.

**Worker** (`worker/coldemail.ts`, ~line 447):
- In the existing success-path `db.coldSend.update(...)` (the same one that already sets `status: "SENT"`, `sentAt`, `messageId`), added `subjectSent: msg.subject` and `bodyHtmlSent: msg.html` from the `RenderedMessage` returned by `buildMessage()` in `lib/coldemail/sender.ts`. No new DB write was added — same update call, same transaction boundary.

**New UI**:
- `components/admin/coldemail/SentEmailViewer.tsx` — a structural copy of `components/admin/EmailLogViewer.tsx`: 3-card stats row (Sent shown below + preview-available count, Open rate, Click rate — same `pct()`/denominator logic), a table (Time/To/Subject/[Campaign when unfiltered]/Status/Opened/Clicked/Preview), and a `createPortal`-into-`document.body` modal with a `sandbox=""` iframe. Includes a local `stripTrackingPixel()` that mirrors `EmailLogViewer`'s function in behavior/purpose but targets cold email's actual pixel endpoint (`/api/coldemail/track/open/...` from `openPixelUrl()` in `lib/coldemail/sender.ts`, vs the transactional mailer's `/api/track/email/...`) — I did not touch `EmailLogViewer.tsx` itself to avoid conflicting with other agents editing shared files. Rows with null `subject`/`html` (legacy sends) render "—" and a "Not available" label instead of a Preview button, per spec.
- `app/admin/coldemail/sent/page.tsx` — new top-level page, `requireArea("platform")` gated (same pattern as every other `app/admin/coldemail/*` page), fetches `ColdSend` rows (`status: "SENT"`, optional `campaignId` filter) joined to `contact.email` and `campaign.name`, up to 200 rows, passed to `SentEmailViewer`.
- `lib/admin-groups.ts` — added a `"Sent"` tab (`/admin/coldemail/sent`) to the existing `coldemail-campaigns` nav group, alongside `Campaigns` and `Templates`.

**Placement decision**: I put this at a new top-level page rather than a campaign-detail sub-tab. The campaign detail page (`app/admin/coldemail/campaigns/[id]/page.tsx`) has no internal tab structure — it's one long stacked-cards page, unlike `/admin/logs` which uses query-param tabs. The real Cold Email nav pattern (`lib/admin-groups.ts`) is a flat sidebar of grouped top-level routes (e.g. `coldemail-campaigns` already has "Campaigns" + "Templates" as sibling pages), so a new `/admin/coldemail/sent` route with a campaign-filter dropdown (defaulting to "All campaigns", avoiding the firehose problem) fit that established pattern best. When no campaign filter is applied, an extra Campaign column is shown so rows stay identifiable — the only deviation from the literal column list in the spec, added for usability in the global view.

**Verification**: `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with no errors after both the schema and UI changes. Did not run `npm run build` (shared-tree build-lock caution honored). No commits made.
